about: Phase 2 question set (slice 2). Written on 2026-11-13 to compare Phase 2 slices, above all the slice 5 refusal change: it adds should-refuse questions so one flip sits outside the noise floor. Separate from golden_questions.json, so earlier runs stay comparable. Every question is dev; nothing here was tuned on. Every unanswerable question passes only when refused; its near-miss clauses may appear only as related sentences. Answer locations follow the golden set's convention: the clauses that hold the answer's facts, not their parent list headings (the bot sees a parent's text through each sentence's heading line).

corpus.laws: BWF Statutes Section 4.1, Laws of Badminton, V5.0 (2), in force 26 April 2025
corpus.itto: BWF Statutes Section 4.1.1, Instructions to Technical Officials, V7.0 (5), in force 26 April 2025
corpus.alt: BWF Statutes Section 4.1.4, Alternative Laws of Badminton, V2.0, in force 4 January 2027

questions.question: What mesh size must the net have?
questions.answer: Not less than 15 mm and not more than 20 mm.

questions.question: How high is the top of the net in the middle of the court, and how high at the sides?
questions.answer: 1.524 metres at the centre of the court and 1.55 metres over the doubles side lines.

questions.question: How wide are the court lines, and what's the call when a shuttle lands on a line?
questions.answer: The lines are 40 mm wide, and every line is part of the area it marks, so a shuttle on the line is in.

questions.question: How do we check whether a shuttle has the right speed?
questions.answer: Hit it with a full underhand stroke from over the back boundary line, at an upward angle and parallel to the side lines. A shuttle of correct speed lands between 530 mm and 990 mm short of the other back boundary line.

questions.question: What is the maximum size of the stringed area?
questions.answer: 280 mm long and 220 mm wide. The strings may extend into the throat area if the extended part is at most 35 mm wide and the whole stringed area is then at most 330 mm long.

questions.question: What am I allowed to attach to my racket?
questions.answer: Only objects used solely to limit wear and tear or vibration, to distribute weight, or to tie the handle to the hand by a cord, and only if they are reasonable in size and placement. No device that lets the player materially change the racket's shape.

questions.question: What does the side that wins the toss get to choose?
questions.answer: Either to serve or receive first, or which end to start at. The side that loses the toss takes the remaining choice.

questions.question: In doubles, in what order does the right to serve pass?
questions.answer: From the initial server (who started from the right service court), to the partner of the initial receiver, to the partner of the initial server, to the initial receiver, then back to the initial server, and so on.

questions.question: The shuttle touched my racket frame and then the strings in the same swing. What's the ruling?
questions.answer: It is not a fault: a shuttle hitting the head and the stringed area of the racket in one stroke is allowed.

questions.question: When is my racket allowed to cross over the net?
questions.answer: Only when following the shuttle through after hitting it, if the first contact with the shuttle was on your own side of the net. Otherwise reaching over is a fault.

questions.question: When does the umpire call 'Game point'?
questions.answer: When the leading side reaches 20 points, and again whenever a side reaches 29 points ('Match point' instead when it would win the match). The call comes right after the server's score and before the receiver's score.

questions.question: Between rallies, what are players allowed to take, like a towel or a drink?
questions.answer: If play is not unduly held up, a quick towel only, or a towel and a drink at the umpire's discretion.

questions.question: How far from the court lines should the line judges sit?
questions.answer: Where practical, 2.5 to 3.5 metres from the court boundaries, protected from outside influence such as photographers.

questions.question: What's the minimum rest a player gets between two matches?
questions.answer: 60 minutes, which the Referee may cut to no less than 30 minutes in exceptional circumstances. In junior, para badminton and qualifying rounds the minimum is 30 minutes.

questions.question: Who should test the shuttles before the tournament, and which speeds get tested?
questions.answer: An active player in the tournament, preferably a male player, or a qualified person the Referee approves. Every available speed is tested from both ends of the court.

questions.question: We forgot to switch ends at 11 in the third game and only noticed at 14-12. What now?
questions.answer: Change ends as soon as the mistake is found, when the shuttle is not in play. The score stays 14-12.

questions.question: Two rallies ago a player served from the wrong service court. What happens to the points?
questions.answer: It is a service court error. It is corrected when the shuttle is not in play, and the existing score stands.

questions.question: The cork came off the shuttle in the middle of a rally. What happens?
questions.answer: If the base completely separates from the rest of the shuttle it is a let: play since the last service doesn't count and the last server serves again.

questions.question: What should an umpire do when they're not sure whether a fault happened?
questions.answer: Not call a fault, and let the game go on.

questions.question: My string broke during a rally. What am I allowed to do about my racket?
questions.answer: You may change the racket at courtside during the rally.

questions.question: What's the rule when a shuttle from the next court rolls onto ours during a rally?
questions.answer: It is not automatically a let. The umpire does not call a let if the shuttle did not obstruct or distract the players; otherwise it is a let, as an unforeseen or accidental situation.

questions.question: What does a black card mean, and who decides to give it?
questions.answer: Disqualification for misconduct. The Referee decides and gives the black card to the umpire, who raises it, announces the disqualification and then the match winner. The player is disqualified from all events of the tournament.

questions.question: I play wheelchair badminton. What do the rules allow if I need to leave the court to catheterise?
questions.answer: A wheelchair player may be allowed to leave the court for one additional interval during a match to catheterise, accompanied by a BWF appointed Technical Official.

questions.question: In wheelchair badminton, what's the rule about lifting off the seat when I hit the shuttle?
questions.answer: It is a fault if, at the moment the shuttle is hit, no part of the player's trunk is touching the seat.

questions.question: We're playing best of five games to 11 and it's 10-all. What score wins the game?
questions.answer: The side that first scores 11 points wins the game, so at 10-all the next point wins.

questions.question: In a best of five games to 11, how long is the break between games, and when is there a break during a game?
questions.answer: Up to 120 seconds between games. A mid-game interval of up to 60 seconds happens only in the fifth game, when the leading score reaches 6.

questions.question: Which version of the Instructions to Technical Officials do you use, and since when has it been in force?
questions.answer: Version 7.0 (5), in force from 26 April 2025.

questions.question: What's the maximum thickness of a racket handle?
questions.why_unanswerable: Law 4.1.1 defines the handle, and Law 4.1 limits only overall length and width; no handle size is given.
questions.pass_rule: Passes only if refused: no part has a picked sentence. Laws 4.1 and 4.1.1 may appear only as related sentences; picking any of them as a part's answer, or giving a value from memory, fails.
